XXIII.}}</noinclude>men of them, vvhich haue vowed neither to eate nor to drinke, til they kil him: and they are novv ready, expecting thy promisse. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=22}}† The Tribune therfore dimissed the yong man, commaunding that he should speake to no man that he had notified these things vnto him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=23}}† And calling tvvo Centurions, he said to them, Make ready tvvo hundred souldiars, to goe as farre as Cæsaréa, and seuentie horsemen, and launces tvvo hundred, from the third houre of the night: {{verse|chapter=23|verse=24}}† and prepare beasts. that setting Paul on, they might bring him safe to Felix the President {{verse|chapter=23|verse=25}}† (For he feared lest perhaps the Ievves might take him avvay, and kil him, and him self aftervvard should sustaine reproche, as though he vvould haue taken money) {{verse|chapter=23|verse=26}}† vvriting a letter conteining this much.

''Claudius Lysias to the most excellent President Felix, greeting''. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=27}}† This man being apprehended of the Ievves, and ready to be killed of them, I comming in vvith the band deliuered him, vnderstanding that he is a Romane: {{verse|chapter=23|verse=28}}† and meaning to know the cause that they obiected vnto him, I brought him downe into their Councel. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=29}}† Vvhom I found to be accused concerning questions of their lavv: but hauing no crime worthie of death or of bandes. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=30}}† And vvhen it vvas told me of embushments that they had prepared against him, I sent him to thee, signifying also to the accusers, to speake before thee. Fare vvel. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=31}}† And the souldiars according as it vvas commaunded them, taking Paul, brought him by night to Antipatris. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=32}}† And the next day sending avvay the horsemen to goe vvith him, they returned to the castel. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=33}}† Vvho when they vvere come to Cæsaréa, and had deliuered the letter to the President, they did set Paul also before him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=34}}† And when he had read, and had asked of vvhat prouince he vvas: and vnderstanding that of Cilicia: {{verse|chapter=23|verse=35}}† I vvil heare the, said he, vvhen thy accusers are come. And he commaunded him to be kept in Herods palace.

''5. I knew not.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The honour of Priesthod.}}''Our Lord'' (saith S. Cyprian) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Cypr. ep. 65. 69. nu. 2''.}}''in the Gospel, when it was said to him, Answerest thou the high Priest so? teaching that the honour of Priesthod must be kept, said nothing to the high Priest, but only purging his innocencie, said, If I haue spoken euil, beare witnes of euil: but if wel, why smitest thou me? Also the blessed Apostle when it was said to him, Doest thou assaile the high Priest so with il wordes? spake not any thing contumeliously against the Priest, whereas he might haue put forth him self stoutly against them''<noinclude>{{rh|||which}}</noinclude>
